hypothesis: A frozen Jev policy-stance filter improves a simple FOMC rate-action rule after assumed costs.
events: All regular FOMC policy statements in the official calendar, 2021-2025. Strategy-framework statements excluded by title, not outcomes.
baseline: Buy USD on an announced target-rate increase, sell on a decrease, otherwise remain flat.
primaryTreatment: Keep a baseline trade only if Jev stance agrees with its direction and the selected classification probability is at least 0.70. This probability is NOT a trading win probability.
secondaryDiagnostic: Jev stance alone determines direction; not the primary hypothesis and not eligible for post-hoc promotion.
jevQuestion: Classify the current statement's explicit policy stance as hawkish, dovish, or neutral/mixed. Previous statement provided as context. Do not predict prices or rely on historical knowledge.
executionProxy: First non-missing FRED DEXJPUS fixing strictly after the announcement date; exit at the next available fixing. These are ex-post reference rates, not executable broker prices or a real-time feed.

costAssumptions.meaning: Illustrative stress assumptions, NOT measured broker spreads, swaps, or billed API charges. One USDJPY pip = JPY 0.01 per USD.

missingInference: Abort the performance comparison; never silently omit failures or treat them as successful abstention.
successGate: No live-trading approval from this probe. Compare cost-adjusted PnL and closed-equity drawdown, report trade counts and paired bootstrap uncertainty. Positive historical results only justify a separately approved prospective paper trial.
knownLimitations: Model training contamination cannot be excluded
Current-vintage FRED data may be revised
FRED is published with a lag, not a live broker feed
Market expectations and surprises not modeled
No operation or outage resilience evidence
No parameter search or retuning in this run
